text: The lab results show significant elevations in Alkaline Phosphatase, AST, and ALT, while the ultrasound reveals an enlarged, thin-walled gallbladder without stones. The CBC results show normal white blood cell counts, which makes an acute infectious process like cholangitis less likely given your symptoms. Given your history of heavy alcohol use, smoking, and the ultrasound findings of an enlarged gallbladder without stones, have you experienced any episodes of severe abdominal pain radiating to your back, suggesting pancreatitis?

speaker: Doctor
text:
The normal amylase results rule out acute pancreatitis, and your ultrasound showing an enlarged, thin-walled gallbladder with no stones, combined with significantly elevated ALP and your history of heavy alcohol use and smoking, is highly suggestive of a malignancy involving the gallbladder or biliary tree. Have you noticed any pain specifically in your right upper quadrant, or any changes in the size of your abdomen?
